# my-flow v0.1.0 - working agreement

my-flow is a thin workflow layer on top of the native features of this tool. It adds no runtime
and no external tools: just a four-stage flow, a set of skills, a few subagent roles, and a
`specs/` + `changes/` directory layout as the durable record of intent. Everything below is a
convention, not a state machine.

## 1. Operating principles

- Work directly by default. Delegate to a subagent only when it materially improves quality,
  speed, or independence of judgment (review, verification, second opinion).
- Evidence over assumption. Read the code before describing it; run the command before
  claiming its result. Newer evidence overrides older hypotheses.
- Ask only when the next step is irreversible, credential-gated, production-facing, or would
  materially change scope. Otherwise choose the safest reasonable interpretation and proceed.
- Surgical diffs: every changed line traces back to the request. No drive-by refactors, no
  new dependencies, no new abstractions unless asked.
- Check official documentation before using an unfamiliar SDK, engine API, or CLI flag.

## 2. The four-stage flow

`interview -> mf-plan -> execute -> mf-verify`. Each stage consumes the previous stage's
artifact. (The mf- prefixed skills are deliberately distinct from the built-in `/plan`, `run`, and
`verify` commands.)

| Request looks like | Stages to use |
|---|---|
| Concrete, single file, clear acceptance | `execute` only (or just do it) |
| Concrete, multi-file or multi-module | `mf-plan -> execute -> mf-verify` |
| Concrete, multi-file, design already clear | `mf-plan --fast [--go] -> execute -> mf-verify` |
| Vague, no acceptance criteria, or "should we..." | `interview -> mf-plan -> execute -> mf-verify` |
| Touches build config, shaders, engine modules, migrations, auth | never skip `mf-plan` and `mf-verify` |

Rules:
- `interview` asks one question per round and stops when non-goals and decision boundaries
  are explicit. Do not re-open the interview inside `mf-plan`.
- `mf-plan` never implements. `execute` never redesigns; if the design is wrong, stop and
  go back.
- `mf-plan --fast` is a fast lane the user asks for (one critic pass, no planner or
  architect); the model never selects it, and it is never used for the high-risk row.
- `mf-verify` runs in a separate context from the one that wrote the code.
- Skills: /my-flow:interview, /my-flow:mf-plan, /my-flow:execute, /my-flow:mf-verify, /my-flow:ask,
  /my-flow:learn, /my-flow:spec, /my-flow:mf-audit. When the user says "interview me", "plan this
  change", "run the change", "verify the change", "ask codex/claude", "make this a skill", or
  "audit the spec", use the matching my-flow skill (not the built-in `/plan`, `run`, or `verify`).

## 3. The intent layer (specs/ and changes/)

Structure borrowed from OpenSpec; no external tool is involved. /my-flow:spec handles
`new / status / validate / abandon / archive / stage`.

- `specs/<capability>/spec.md` is the current truth about behavior (requirements with
  WHEN / THEN scenarios).
- `changes/<name>/` holds the intent for one change: `proposal.md` (why, what, non-goals,
  decision boundaries), `design.md` (how), `tasks.md` (ordered checklist), and optional delta
  specs under `changes/<name>/specs/<capability>/spec.md` (ADDED / MODIFIED / REMOVED).
- Delta-first: write specs only for behavior that this change adds or modifies.
- `tasks.md` checkboxes (`- [ ] 1.1 ... and verify ...`) are the only progress ledger. Tick a
  box only after that task's own verification passed. Never keep progress anywhere else.
- `design.md` must contain these two sections, even if the answer is "none":
  - `## Do-Not-Touch` - modules, directories, or files this change must not modify.
  - `## Rebuild / Re-run After Change` - what must be regenerated, rebuilt, cooked, or re-run
    after the edit (project files, build targets, caches, test suites).
- When every box is ticked and `mf-verify` passed, `/my-flow:spec archive <name>` merges the
  delta specs into `specs/` and moves the change to `changes/archive/`.
- Simplified fallback for small projects: one `docs/changes/<name>.md` with the same sections.

## 4. Tool-specific notes

Claude Code is the primary interactive executor.
- Agent teams are enabled via `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1` in `settings.json`
  (`env`). On Windows teammates run in-process only; do not ask for split panes.
- One loop authority per session: at most one active `/goal` and at most one team. `execute`
  prints the `/goal` statement, then waits for the user to paste it, for every run
  including one entered from `mf-plan --fast --go`; it never tries to set it itself. The
  Stop hook is only a backstop: during stage `execute` it blocks a completion
  claim that leaves unticked, unblocked tasks, and only while the state file (written by
  `spec stage`) is younger than 12 hours. Plain answers are never blocked.
- Start a team only when `design.md` lists two or more disjoint file-ownership groups.
  Teammates edit only files they own and report back through the shared task list.
- For risky changes, work in a worktree (`claude -w <name>`), or give a subagent
  `isolation: worktree`.
- Subagent roles provided by this plugin: `my-flow:planner`, `my-flow:architect`,
  `my-flow:critic`, `my-flow:verifier`. Architect, critic, and verifier are read-only.

## 5. Verification and completion

- No fresh evidence means not complete. "Should work", "probably passes", and remembered
  results from earlier in the session are not evidence.
- Placeholder TODOs, `test.skip` / `.only`, stub returns, and unimplemented branches are
  blockers, not progress. Inspect changed files for them before claiming completion.
- The writer and the verifier are separate passes. Never approve work in the same context
  that produced it.
- Final gate, in order: (1) targeted verification of the change, (2) cleanup of your own
  diff only, (3) re-verify, (4) independent review (/my-flow:mf-verify or /my-flow:ask),
  (5) declare done and tick the last box.

## 6. Cross-model rules

- Use /my-flow:ask for a second opinion on a design, a review of a diff before the final
  gate, a tie-break when plan review stalls, or unfamiliar API behavior. Never for
  implementation.
- The other model runs read-only. Its output is advice, recorded under `.my-flow/ask/`.
- Disagreements are resolved by evidence or by the user, never by majority.

## 7. Paths

- `.my-flow/` is disposable scratch: `ask/`, `interviews/`, `verify/`, `learned/`, `state/`.
  It is git-ignored and may vanish with a worktree; nothing authoritative lives there.
- Durable intent lives only in `specs/` and `changes/` (committed) and in promoted skills
  under `.claude/skills/` and `.agents/skills/` (committed).
